video_title: Lexie Brown Confronts Michael Porter Jr. Over His WNBA Comments, Caitlin Clark & Player Pay

quotes.speaker: Lexie Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: Lexie Brown criticizes the WNBA's narrative regarding player pay and value
quotes.excerpt: There's money to be made. There's an appetite for women's basketball. And the league just kept telling us
quotes.quote: The narrative they put out was so weird. It was so annoying. There's money to be made. There's an appetite for women's basketball. And the league just kept telling us, you guys are asking for too much. You're asking for too much.

quotes.speaker: Michael Porter Jr.
quotes.summary_phrase: Michael Porter Jr. apologizes for his previous comments about WNBA players
quotes.excerpt: I want to start this interview by just apologizing for the way that I have come off
quotes.quote: I want to start this interview by just apologizing for the way that I have come off, not only to you, but I feel like I rubbed even other NBA players the wrong way. I have my opinions and when people ask me questions, I do speak my mind, but I'm not always mindful of how that can come off. I feel like for you guys, when you saw my comments, I don't know, I feel like you might have taken it the wrong way.

quotes.speaker: Lexie Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: Lexie Brown discusses the media's tendency to use clickbait clips
quotes.excerpt: They clipped that specific comment you made about the ping pong, whatever, but like if you listen

text_blocks.text: They clipped that specific comment you made about the ping pong, whatever, but like if you listen to the whole statement that you made and the way they frame the question. Also, there were opportunities for them to be like, okay, that's enough. But they kind of just let you do your thing.

text_blocks.speaker: Lexie Brown
text_blocks.text: I mean, that's what social media is. That's what clickbait is. And they clipped that specific comment you made about the ping pong, whatever, but like if you listen to the whole statement that you made and the way they frame the question. Also, there were opportunities for them to be like, okay, that's enough. But they kind of just let you do your thing. Also, they like to lob me questions for me to potentially be problematic or, you know, because that's what they like to do. They like to poke people and poke the bear. I'm not that type of person. But when you see the clip, you're like, okay, I'm going to ride for my girls. I'm going to ride for my W players. But I do understand the respect you do have for us as players and things like that.

quotes.speaker: Lexie Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: Lexie Brown addresses the link between WNBA player pay and league legitimacy
quotes.excerpt: When people talk about the W, specifically men and other athletes, the legitimacy of our league
quotes.quote: When people talk about the W, specifically men and other athletes, the legitimacy of our league and who we are as players varies based on how much money we make. So the conversation was kind of framed of like, oh, you know, the women they want more money. Like, what's up with that? Like, why do they want more money? And then, you know, the conversation shifts to, oh, they're not exciting enough. They don't dunk, lower the rims, blah, blah, blah, blah, blah.

quotes.speaker: Michael Porter Jr.
quotes.summary_phrase: Michael Porter Jr. clarifies his comments on lowering WNBA rims
quotes.excerpt: To get the viewership up, maybe lower the rims. And I think that that comment rubbed
quotes.quote: To get the viewership up, maybe lower the rims. And I think that that comment rubbed not only you but probably some other WNBA players the wrong way. But my question to you would be like, what about that comment makes it offensive because the ball is smaller, the three-point line is a little bit shorter than the NBA three-point line. So why is lowering the rim a little bit lower than the NBA rim? Why is that one thing so offensive if the ball is shorter, the three-point line is a little shorter? Like what about that is so crazy to you?

quotes.speaker: Lexie Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: Lexie Brown explains why lowering WNBA rims is not a solution
quotes.excerpt: Me personally, like that will not benefit me at all. But so many of us, even with
quotes.quote: Me personally, like that will not benefit me at all. But so many of us, even with the rim lower, like you're still not going to get people dunking on people. And now we have my teammate, Domonique, is dunking. And it's still not enough. Like she's literally dunking by a 10-foot rim in games. She did it overseas, she did it in Unrivaled, and people are still like, oh, that dunk wasn't good enough. Like so you lower the rims and then maybe people start dunking and then they'll be like, well, it's still a 9-foot rim. Like it's still not good enough.

quotes.speaker: Lexie Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: Lexie Brown explains why WNBA players prefer being called women over females
quotes.excerpt: I think it's the context of the way you're saying it. So the whole conversation was very
quotes.quote: I think it's the context of the way you're saying it. So the whole conversation was very kind of talking down on us. And in the experiences that I've had where men call women females, it's like very derogatory, you know? So maybe you weren't, obviously you just explained how you feel about the word female, but in the experiences that probably a lot of us have had when men are like, these females, these this, it's like very derogatory and like just talking down on us.

quotes.speaker: Lexie Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: Lexie Brown discusses the mutual respect between NBA and WNBA players
quotes.excerpt: I think overall like NBA guys, they respect what we do and the way we play because
quotes.quote: I think overall like NBA guys, they respect what we do and the way we play because they understand that we work as hard, we put the same hours in, you know, we've spent our whole lives trying to get to this level. So I think there is a mutual respect amongst NBA players and WNBA players. It's like the casual fans, like again, I said, they put the money, the dollar amount next to the occupation and it's less respected.

quotes.speaker: Lexie Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: Lexie Brown explains why she deleted her social media accounts
quotes.excerpt: As a grown as woman, getting offended by strangers on the internet, I started to feel like
quotes.quote: As a grown as woman, getting offended by strangers on the internet, I started to feel like, okay, you're doing this to yourself. Like you can literally delete the app. Like you might miss out on some jokes, you might be out the loop a little bit, but your mental, I had to value that. So I literally just deleted it and I've never been, I haven't returned yet.

quotes.speaker: Lexie Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: Lexie Brown discusses her recent absence from the WNBA
quotes.excerpt: I haven't really been playing the last three seasons. I have like barely played. I got sick
quotes.quote: I haven't really been playing the last three seasons. I have like barely played. I got sick two years ago. It was dealing with that and then last year I got traded and didn't play. So I really haven't felt the the heat from this new fandom, which I'm kind of grateful for because it's been crazy.

quotes.speaker: Lexie Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: Lexie Brown discusses the unprecedented growth of the WNBA
quotes.excerpt: There was just this explosive growth, like unprecedented growth in the WNBA between, you know, NIL stuff
quotes.quote: There was just this explosive growth, like unprecedented growth in the WNBA between, you know, NIL stuff, the Caitlin Clark, Angel Reese stuff. Like so many things happened in women's sports and like this small moment, it like just took off like crazy. Like no one was prepared for it. Like no one was expecting it.

quotes.speaker: Lexie Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: Lexie Brown explains the WNBA's recent CBA negotiations
quotes.excerpt: We opted out of our CBA and, um, we opted out last year. So we've we got to
quotes.quote: We opted out of our CBA and, um, we opted out last year. So we've we got to an agreement, so we we signed the new CBA, our season's happening, whatever, but it was an 18-month process. So we opted out and the official deadline was like January. So we didn't get it signed until two weeks ago.

quotes.speaker: Lexie Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: Lexie Brown compares WNBA salaries to off-season league earnings
quotes.excerpt: I made more money in Athletes Unlimited this past year than I've made in the WNBA last
quotes.quote: I made more money in Athletes Unlimited this past year than I've made in the WNBA last year. And a lot of players made more money in Unrivaled than they made in the WNBA. So the is there, there's money to be made. There's a there's an appetite for women's basketball. And the league just kept telling us, you guys are asking for too much. You're asking for too much.

quotes.speaker: Lexie Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: Lexie Brown discusses the WNBA's revenue share structure
quotes.excerpt: Our last CBA, we were getting like 9% of rev rev share compared to the owners, compared
quotes.quote: Our last CBA, we were getting like 9% of rev rev share compared to the owners, compared to ownership? Yes. So we were at like 9% and every year it was going down. So we were like, yeah, no, like do you see what's going on with the league right now? Like people are really like messing with the WNBA finally. It took 20-plus years, but we here now, right?

quotes.speaker: Lexie Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: Lexie Brown reflects on her rookie salary in the WNBA
quotes.excerpt: I made like 40k my rookie year. You can't live off 40k. It's not enough to really live
quotes.quote: I made like 40k my rookie year. You can't live off 40k. It's not enough to really live in some of these big, you played in LA? I was drafted to Connecticut. So it was cool there. But yeah, like you think about, you can't live off 40k. So I took my ass overseas immediately. So I played overseas for three straight years.

quotes.speaker: Lexie Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: Lexie Brown discusses the challenges of WNBA player relationships
quotes.excerpt: I've been on multiple teams with players in relationships and sometimes it's good, sometimes it's not so
quotes.quote: I've been on multiple teams with players in relationships and sometimes it's good, sometimes it's not so good. I think it's less about the relationship and more about the people in the relationship. So there's like no like blanket statement to like talk about like what that's like because I had teammates in Chicago who were married and they were amazing.

quotes.speaker: Lexie Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: Lexie Brown discusses the WNBA's inclusive policy for trans athletes
quotes.excerpt: My response is very aligned with our Athletes Unlimited. We have a an inclusive policy.
quotes.quote: My response is very aligned with our Athletes Unlimited. We have a an inclusive policy. I don't know it verbatim, but it's available, it's there. We had a trans, what did he run? He was a track Olympic track athlete. He came in and we had like a whole seminar with him, educated us on all types of stuff and just the benefits of being inclusive. Me personally, I like I stay away from this topic for sure, but the way Athletes Unlimited aligns and stands on that topic, you know, we had a vote on it and and okay it and I think it's good.

quotes.speaker: Lexie Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: Lexie Brown emphasizes the importance of WNBA players getting degrees
quotes.excerpt: I'm always going to promote, you know, the girls to stay in school and get their degree
quotes.quote: I'm always going to promote, you know, the girls to stay in school and get their degree, whatever, make your money. Um, you know, there's always been some pushback of like lowering the draft age and all that stuff, which I'm like, if we lower the draft age, cool, like that doesn't mean you have to enter the draft, but if it's the option, cool. But I'm always like, go get your degree. Like at the end of the day, we're women. Our careers are shorter. We're still not making that much money. Like once the ball stops bouncing, like you need something to fall back on.

text_blocks.text: I think I just get asked questions and I'm just like, well, I'm getting asked, so I'm going to get my opinion. But people rage bait, people do things for clicks and I'm aware of it.

text_blocks.text: Sometimes I feel like I get treated like you get treated in the WNBA community. Especially once I started going on Gills, it was always something.

text_blocks.speaker: Michael Porter Jr.
text_blocks.text: I wasn't locked into your opinions much on what you were saying, but so you know how it feels. If the WNBA told you, you can't...

text_blocks.text: Well, I will say when I first got into the league, I was on YouTube, I was vlogging, I was doing all that stuff. And they didn't straight up, the thing about, because the thing I can respect about the conversation that Brooklyn had with you is that they brought you in and let you know, okay, we see what you're doing. quotes.speaker: Lexie Brown

quotes.excerpt: I got waived in the off-season. It just wasn't worth it for you like that, yeah.

text_blocks.speaker: Lexie Brown
text_blocks.text: The shit I was dealing with was, no one was telling me that it was a problem, but I kept getting things were happening in my career that had nothing to do with basketball, but no one was having a conversation with me about it. So it did get to a point where I stopped vlogging. I shut my whole YouTube shit down, because then after I got waived, I got waived in the off-season.

text_blocks.speaker: Michael Porter Jr.
text_blocks.text: It just wasn't worth it for you like that, yeah.

text_blocks.speaker: Lexie Brown
text_blocks.text: No conversation, no nothing. To this day, I still don't know why I got waived from the Minnesota Lynx. I have no idea. The coach didn't call me, the GM, nobody called me. I found out through my agent.

quotes.speaker: Michael Porter Jr.
quotes.summary_phrase: Michael Porter Jr. on the disposable nature of young NBA players
quotes.excerpt: if you're a young dude who was first getting in the NBA, they will wave you quick

text_blocks.speaker: Michael Porter Jr.
text_blocks.text: If it was a young dude who was first getting in the NBA, and he was a TikTok guy or he was doing a podcast and he was speaking his opinions and he didn't make his mark in the league yet, they will wave you quick, because you haven't made a mark, you're not a, you're not a, you're disposable at the end of the day. But I think if you're a certain level of a player, like if you're a Jaylen Brown, he could go on a stream and say probably whatever, he's not going nowhere. It's Jaylen Brown, he's one of the best players in the NBA. I think it's tough in Jaden Ivey's situation, because if it was probably before he had his surgery, he was still in Detroit, balling, one of their franchise guys, they probably would have called him in, but if you're not one of the main guys on a team, they'll get rid of you.

text_blocks.speaker: Lexie Brown
text_blocks.text: And you learn that quickly in the pro.

quotes.speaker: Lexie Brown

text_blocks.text: With the protection of these rookies, like we see the brands that they're building in college. We see the personalities that they have in college, and so many of us in the majority of the league have seen so many personalities and amazing players get stomped out because they don't fit the mold, right? So none of these new rookies are fitting whatever stupid ass mold existed 10 years ago in the W. And we wanted to protect them from that. So now you're getting all this money, you know, up front, so teams have to be intentional with choosing you for your team.

text_blocks.speaker: Michael Porter Jr.
text_blocks.text: Yeah, no, y'all are definitely lit and I'm excited to see it keep growing.
